text:
The maximum value of the term independent of 't' in the expansion 
of $\left (tx^{\frac{1}{5}}+\frac{(1-x)^{\dfrac{1}{10}}}{t}\right )^{10}$ where x$\in$(0, 1) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$T_{r+1}={}^{10}C_{r}(tx^{1/5})^{10-r}\left [\frac{(1-x)^{1/10}}{t}\right ]^{r}$

$={}^{10}C_{r}t^{(10-2r)}\times x^{\frac{10-r}{5}}\times (1-x)^{\frac{r}{10}}$

$\Rightarrow 10-2r=0\Rightarrow r=5$

$\therefore$ $T_{6}={}^{10}C_{5}\times x\sqrt{1-x}$

At maximum, $\frac{dT_{6}}{dx}={}^{10}C_{5}\left [\sqrt{1-x}-\frac{x}{2\sqrt{1-x}}\right ]=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $1-x=x/2\Rightarrow 3x=2\Rightarrow x=2/3$

$T_{6}|_{\max }=\frac{10!}{5!5!}\times \frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}$ = $\frac{2.10!}{3\sqrt{3}(5!)^{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text: The value of $\lim _{h\to 0}2\left \{\frac{\sqrt{3}\sin \left (\frac{π}{6}+h\right )-\cos \left (\frac{π}{6}+h\right )}{\sqrt{3}h\left (\sqrt{3}\cosh -\sinh \right )}\right \}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let L = $\lim _{h\to 0}2\left \{\frac{\sqrt{3}\sin \left (\frac{π}{6}+h\right )-\cos \left (\frac{π}{6}+h\right )}{\sqrt{3}h\left (\sqrt{3}\cosh -\sinh \right )}\right \}$

$\Rightarrow$ L = $\lim _{h\to 0}2\times 2\left \{\frac{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin \left (\frac{π}{6}+h\right )-\frac{1}{2}\cos \left (\frac{π}{6}+h\right )}{2\sqrt{3}h\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cosh -\frac{1}{2}\sinh \right )}\right \}$

$\Rightarrow$ L = $\lim _{h\to 0}2\times 2\left \{\frac{\cos \frac{π}{6}\sin \left (\frac{π}{6}+h\right )-\sin \frac{π}{6}\cos \left (\frac{π}{6}+h\right )}{2\sqrt{3}h\left (\cos \frac{π}{6}\cosh -\sin \frac{π}{6}\sinh \right )}\right \}$

$\Rightarrow$ L = $\lim _{h\to 0}2\times 2\left \{\frac{\sin \left (\frac{π}{6}+h-\frac{π}{6}\right )}{2\sqrt{3}h\cos \left (h+\frac{π}{6}\right )}\right \}$

$\Rightarrow$ L = $\frac{4}{2\sqrt{3}}\lim _{h\to 0}\left \{\frac{\sin (h)}{h\cos \left (h+\frac{π}{6}\right )}\right \}$

$\Rightarrow$ L = $\frac{4}{2\sqrt{3}}\times \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ = $\frac{4}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text: Let A be a symmetric matrix of order 2 with integer entries. If the sum of the diagonal elements of $A^{2}$ is 1, then the possible number of such matrices is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ b & c \end{array}\right ]$

$A^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ b & c \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ b & c \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a^{2}+b^{2} & ab+bc \\ ab+bc & c^{2}+b^{2} \end{array}\right ]$

$=a^{2}+2b^{2}+c^{2}=1$

$a=1,b=0,c=0$

$a=0,b=0,c=1$

$a=-1,b=0,c=0$

$c=-1,b=0,a=0$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text: The value of $\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}\frac{\cos ^{2}x}{1+3^{x}}dx$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $I=\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{2}}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{\cos ^{2}x}{1+3^{x}}dx$ .... (1)

Replace x with $-$x,

$\therefore$ $I=\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{2}}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{\cos ^{2}x}{1+\frac{1}{3x}}$ .... (2)

Adding (1) and (2), we get,

$2I=\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{2}}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{\cos ^{2}x+3^{x}\cos ^{2}x}{1+3^{x}}dx$

$=\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{2}}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{\cos ^{2}x(1+3^{x})}{1+3^{x}}dx$

$=\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{2}}^{\frac{π}{2}}\cos ^{2}xdx$

[$\cos ^{2}x$ is a even function as $f(x)=f(-x)$ for $\cos ^{2}x$]

$=2\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\cos ^{2}xdx$

$=2\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\left (\frac{1+\cos 2x}{2}\right )dx$

$\Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}(1+\cos 2x)dx$

$=\frac{1}{2}[x+\sin 2x]_{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}$

$=\frac{1}{2}\left [\frac{π}{2}-0\right ]$

$=\frac{π}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text: The number of seven digit integers with sum of the digits equal to 10 and formed by using the digits 1, 2 and 3 only is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(I) First possibility is 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3

required number = $\frac{7!}{5!}$ = 7 $\times$ 6 = 42

(II) Second possibility is 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2

required number = $\frac{7!}{4!3!}=\frac{7\times 6\times 5}{6}=35$

Total = 42 + 35 = 77

text: Let R = {(P, Q) | P and Q are at the same distance from the origin} be a relation, then the equivalence class of (1, $-$1) is the set :

text: The value of $\sum\limits _{n=1}^{100}\int\limits _{n-1}^{n}e^{x-[x]}dx$, where [ x ] is the greatest integer $\leq$ x, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\sum\limits _{n=1}^{100}\int\limits _{n-1}^{n}e^{x-[x]}dx$

Here, $n-1\leq x<n$

$\therefore$ $[x]=n-1$

$\therefore$ $\int\limits _{n-1}^{n}e^{x-(n-1)}dx$

$=\left [e^{x-(n-1)}\right ]_{n-1}^{n}$

$=e^{1}-e^{0}$

$=e-1$

Now, $\sum\limits _{n=1}^{100}(e-1)=100(e-1)$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text:
If $\frac{\sin ^{-1}x}{a}=\frac{\cos ^{-1}x}{b}=\frac{\tan ^{-1}y}{c}$; $0<x<1$, 
then the value of $\cos \left (\frac{πc}{a+b}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{\sin ^{-1}x}{a}=\frac{\cos ^{-1}x}{b}=\frac{\tan ^{-1}y}{c}$

$\frac{\sin ^{-1}x}{a}=\frac{\cos ^{-1}x}{b}=\frac{\sin ^{-1}x+\cos ^{-1}x}{a+b}=\frac{π}{2(a+b)}$

Now, $\frac{\tan ^{-1}y}{c}=\frac{π}{2(a+b)}$

$2\tan ^{-1}y=\frac{πc}{a+b}$

$\Rightarrow \cos \left (\frac{πc}{a+b}\right )=\cos (2\tan ^{-1}y)=\frac{1-y^{2}}{1+y^{2}}$

text: The maximum slope of the curve $y=\frac{1}{2}x^{4}-5x^{3}+18x^{2}-19x$ occurs at the point :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $y=\frac{1}{2}x^{4}-5x^{3}+18x^{2}-19x$

$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{2}\times 4x^{3}-15x^{2}+36x-19$

$\Rightarrow$ Slope M = $2x^{3}-15x^{2}+36x-19$

At max of slope $\frac{dM}{dx}=0$

$\therefore$ $\frac{dM}{dx}=6x^{2}-30x+36=0$

$\Rightarrow 6(x^{2}-5x+6)=0$

$\Rightarrow 6(x-2)(x-3)=0$

$\therefore$ $x=2,3$

Now, $\frac{d^{2}M}{dx^{2}}=6(2x-5)$

at $x=2,\frac{d^{2}M}{dx^{2}}=6(4-5)=-6<0$

$\therefore$ at x = 2 slope is maximum.

At x = 2,

y = 8 - 40 + 72 - 38 = 2

$\therefore$ Required point = (2, 2)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text: The rate of growth of bacteria in a culture is proportional to the number of bacteria present and the bacteria count is 1000 at initial time t = 0. The number of bacteria is increased by 20% in 2 hours. If the population of bacteria is 2000 after $\frac{k}{\log _{e}\left (\frac{6}{5}\right )}$ hours, then $\left (\frac{k}{\log _{e}2}\right )^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dx}{dt}\propto x$

$\frac{dx}{dt}=λx$

$\int\limits _{1000}^{x}\frac{dx}{x}=\int\limits _{0}^{t}λdt$

$\ln x-\ln 1000=λt$

$\ln \left (\frac{x}{1000}\right )=λt$

Put t = 2, x = 1200

$\ln \left (\frac{12}{10}\right )=2λ\Rightarrow λ=\frac{1}{2}\ln \frac{6}{5}$

Now, $\ln \left (\frac{x}{1000}\right )=\frac{t}{2}\ln \left (\frac{6}{5}\right )$

$x=1000e^{\frac{t}{2}\ln \left (\frac{6}{5}\right )}$

$x=2000$ at $t=\frac{k}{\ln \left (\frac{6}{5}\right )}$

$\Rightarrow 2000=1000e^{\frac{k}{2\ln (6/5)}\times \ln (6/5)}$

$\Rightarrow 2=e^{k/2}$

$\Rightarrow \ln 2=\frac{k}{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{k}{\ln 2}=2$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{k}{\ln 2}\right )^{2}=4$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text: The number of solutions of the equation $\log _{4}(x$ $-$ $1) = \log _{2}(x$ $-$ 3) is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\log _{4}(x-1)=\log _{2}(x-3)$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}\log _{2}(x-1)=\log _{2}(x-3)$

$\Rightarrow \log _{2}(x-1)^{1/2}=\log _{2}(x-3)$

$\Rightarrow (x-1)^{1/2}=x-3$

$\Rightarrow x-1=x^{2}+9-6x$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}-7x+10=0$

$\Rightarrow (x-2)(x-5)=0$

$\Rightarrow x=2,5$

But x $\neq$ 2 because it is not satisfying the domain of given equation $i.e. \log _{2}(x$ $-$ 3) $\to$ its domain x > 3

finally x is 5

$\therefore$ No. of solutions = 1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text: The difference between degree and order of a differential equation that represents the family of curves given by $y^{2}=a\left (x+\frac{\sqrt{a}}{2}\right )$, a > 0 is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$y^{2}=a\left (x+\frac{\sqrt{a}}{2}\right )$

Differentiating both sides, we get

$2yy^{'}=a$

$y^{2}=2yy^{'}\left (x+\frac{\sqrt{2yy^{'}}}{2}\right )$

$y=2y^{'}\left (x+\frac{\sqrt{yy^{'}}}{\sqrt{2}}\right )$

$y-2xy^{'}=\sqrt{2}y^{'}\sqrt{yy^{'}}$

$\left (y-2x\frac{dy}{dx}\right )^{2}=2y\left (\frac{dy}{dx}\right )^{3}$

D = 3 & O = 1

$\therefore$ D $-$ O = 3 $-$ 1 = 2
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text:
If y = y(x) is the solution of the equation 

$e^{\sin y}\cos y\frac{dy}{dx}+e^{\sin y}\cos x=\cos x$, y(0) = 0; then 

$1+y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$e^{\sin  y} \cos  y\frac{dy}{dx}$ $+ e^{\sin  y} \cos  x = \cos  x$

Put $e^{\sin  y} = t$

$e^{\sin  y}$ $\times$ cos y$\frac{dy}{dx}$ = $\frac{dt}{dx}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dt}{dx}$ + t cos x = cos x

I. F. = $e^{\int \cos xdx}=e^{\sin x}$

Solution of differential equation :

$t.e^{\sin x}=\int e^{\sin x}.\cos xdx$

$e^{\sin y}.e^{\sin x}=e^{\sin x}+c$

at x = 0, y = 0

1 = 1 + c $\Rightarrow$ c = 0

$\therefore$ $e^{\sin  x + \sin  y} = e^{\sin  x}$

$\Rightarrow$ sin x + sin y = sin x

$\Rightarrow$ sin y = 0 $\Rightarrow$ y = 0

$\Rightarrow y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )=0,y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )=0,y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=0$

$\therefore$ $1+y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )$

= 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 1
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text: The number of integral values of 'k' for which the equation $3\sin x+4\cos x=k+1$ has a solution, k$\in$R is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

$-\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\leq a\cos x+b\sin x\leq \sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}$

$\therefore$ $-\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}\leq 3\cos x+4\sin x\leq \sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}$

$-5\leq k+1\leq 5$

$-6\leq k\leq 4$

$\therefore$ Set of integers = $-6,-5,-4,-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4$ = Total 11 intergers.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift
